title: Engineering Term (v1, rev. 2)
description: A single entry in the Persian engineering terminology dictionary. Uniqueness of id/slug and referential integrity of related_terms are enforced by scripts/build_pages.py at build time. rev. 2 (2026-09-10) adds optional etymology/root, plural, alias, translation-note and review-level fields and richer reference objects; every new field is optional, so rev. 1 records stay valid.

id.description: Stable, unique identifier for the term (must never change once published).

term_fr.description: French equivalent (unverified translations must stay null).

term_de.description: German equivalent (unverified translations must stay null).

term_ar.description: Arabic equivalent (unverified translations must stay null).

pos.description: Part of speech of the Persian term.

domain.description: Engineering domains; every value must exist in data/terms/_meta.yaml.

definition_fa.description: Persian definition. Target: at least 50 characters (80 once the entry leaves draft); shorter definitions are flagged by the build until content review is complete.

synonyms.description: Persian (or established loanword) synonyms that must also match this entry in search.

usage_examples.description: Short Persian sentences showing the term in real technical use (spec/report/site register).

references.description: Sources backing the definition (standards, books, ...). Every code must exist in data/standards.yaml — an unverifiable citation fails the content gate.

related_terms.description: Ids of related terms; every value must reference an existing term id.

root_fa.description: Persian base/root the term is built from (e.g. 'بند' for آب‌بندی and بندکشی). Powers root-based search and the 'هم‌ریشه‌ها' (same-root) grouping on every page.

root_ar.description: Arabic radical (root letters) of a loanword or of an Arabic base inside a Persian derivative, e.g. 'ق-و-م' for مقاومت, 'ر-ق-م' for رقمی. Write it either hyphen- or tatweel-separated. Meaningful for Arabic-derived vocabulary only.

etymology_fa.description: Human-readable Persian etymology note: origin language, morphological formation, loan-word or trade-jargon history.

origin_lang.description: Language the headword itself was borrowed from (fa = native Persian).

plural_fa.description: Plural form used in technical Persian writing (e.g. 'میلگردها', 'مصالح', 'مشخصات').

search_aliases.description: Extra spellings, transliterations or colloquial/site forms that must match this entry in search, beyond synonyms.

translation_notes.description: Per-language editorial note. Required whenever a translation is a descriptive coinage rather than an attested headword: 'unknown' must stay null and 'uncertain' must be declared here.

status.description: Editorial status. draft = not yet reviewed. reviewed = passed the automated content gates plus a documented review (see review_level). published = human specialist sign-off with stable wording.

review_level.description: Who performed the review. ai-assisted = model-assisted and validated by automated gates, no human sign-off yet; expert = a named human specialist; committee = a terminology committee. status published requires expert or committee.

reviewed_by.description: Name/handle of the reviewer (required once status != draft). Model-assisted reviews must say so explicitly — never impersonate a human expert.

reviewed_at.description: ISO date of the last review (YYYY-MM-DD).

slug.description: Stable URL slug; must be unique across all data files.

allOf.$comment: published means a human signed off — an AI-assisted review can never claim it.

code.description: Registry key from data/standards.yaml (e.g. 'ACI 318-19') or an exact book title listed there.

org.description: Issuing body, e.g. 'ACI', 'ASTM', 'INSO', 'فرهنگستان زبان و ادب فارسی'.

section.description: Clause/section/page pointer inside the source, e.g. '§7.6.1' or 'ص ۴۲'.

url.description: Authoritative landing page of the source. Never a DOI placeholder.

note.description: How the source supports this entry (scope alignment, source of wording, ...). Keeps every citation honest and auditable.
